title: add's return value
prompt: `set.add(x)` returns a boolean. What does `false` mean?
options: `x` was already in the set — nothing changed
The add failed due to memory
explanation: `if (!seen.add(x)) return true;` is a slick one-line duplicate detector: add returns false exactly when x was already present.

title: Pick the structure
prompt: You need to know, for each character a-z in a string, how many times it appears. Best fit?
options: `int[26]` count array — fixed tiny key space
explanation: A set can't count, and a HashMap works but is overkill: when keys are 26 lowercase letters, `counts[c - 'a']++` is faster and shorter.

title: Contains duplicate (warm-up)
prompt: Return `true` if any value appears at least twice. This is literally NeetCode #1 — solve it with the `add`-returns-false trick.

solution.explanation: O(n) time, O(n) space. The sort-first alternative is O(n log n) time but O(1) extra space — worth mentioning in interviews.

hints: `seen.add(x)` returns false when x is already in the set.

title: Drill: find the missing number
prompt: From memory: `nums` contains each of 0..n exactly once EXCEPT one number — return it. Build a set of nums, then loop 0..n and return the value that isn't in the set. (n = nums.length)

tests.note: the missing one can be n itself

solution.explanation: Note `i <= nums.length` — the candidates are 0..n inclusive. (The sum formula and XOR give O(1)-space alternatives.)

hints: Candidates run 0..nums.length INCLUSIVE — use `<=` in the second loop.

title: Recall: set operations
prompt: Fill in the insert, membership, delete, and size operations.
code:
Set<Integer> set = new HashSet<>();
set.{{1}}(5);               // insert
boolean has = set.{{2}}(5); // present?
set.{{3}}(5);               // delete
int n = set.{{4}}();        // count
explanation: `add`, `contains`, `remove`, `size` — all O(1) except size is instant. `add` also returns false if the value was already there.

title: Drill: count distinct
prompt: From memory: return the number of DISTINCT values in `nums` (load them into a HashSet and return its size).
hints: Add everything to a set; duplicates collapse. Return `set.size()`.
